title: The Tail End
goal: The last two readings. A view beats a copy — and the wrong window fails loudly.
hints: len() - 2 .. means 'from two-before-the-end, onward'. ..2 means the OPPOSITE end.
Returning &[i32] is a window; returning Vec<i32> is a purchase.
explanation: Range arithmetic reads from both ends: `len()-2..` opens a window on the tail, `..2` on the head — both compile, and only the test knows which end you meant. Between the correct pair, the borrowed view costs nothing (elision ties it to the input) while to_vec() buys a fresh allocation the caller may not need. Return views by default; return owned copies when the caller must outlive the source.
